clue.text: Reckless officer who assists another in plot

indicators.note: in places the officer's letters inside the word for a plot

parts.note: a plot of land can be shown on a map; a map is also a plan
an ADC, aide-de-camp, is an officer assisting a senior officer

explanation.surface: A rash officer helping someone else in a conspiracy.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild, impulsive person is described as hare-brained or reckless.

clue.text: Slow soldier gets old pursuing girl

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A sluggish soldier grows old chasing a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction for a slow tempo.

clue.text: Prepared mince how the Chinese eat it

definitions.text: Prepared mince how the Chinese eat it

indicators.note: prepared food is made ready, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Ground meat cooked the way they eat it in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared' rearranges MINCE HOW; the whole clue describes the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: This stir-fried noodle dish is a staple of Chinese cookery.

clue.text: Job appointment to mark for the future

parts.note: a post is a job
a date is an appointment

explanation.surface: A job interview set to be noted for later.
explanation.definitionFit: To postdate is to write a later date on a cheque or document.

clue.text: Misplaced emphasis is bad form

indicators.note: misplaced letters are put in the wrong positions, so the next word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Stressing the wrong syllable is poor manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad form' looks like a phrase for poor etiquette but defines a deformed shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A misshape is a deformity, a badly made outline.

clue.text: Name shared by Scots kings I, II, III — and X?

definitions.text: Name shared by Scots kings I, II, III — and X?

parts.words: Name shared by Scots kings I, II, III — and X?
parts.note: the numerals look like a sequence of royal regnal numbers, but X is the surname of an American civil rights leader

explanation.surface: A quiz question about Scottish royal names.
explanation.walkthrough: Several medieval kings of Scotland bore this name; the American activist took X as his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Malcolm I–IV ruled Scotland, and the US activist Malcolm X shares the forename.

clue.text: Second old vessel rounding a ship in seaweed

indicators.note: rounding means the old vessel goes around the other letters

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek legend
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A second ancient vessel circling a ship caught in weed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sargasso is a floating brown weed that gives the Sargasso Sea its name.

clue.text: Chap endlessly unwell on a W. I. island

indicators.note: endlessly means the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Angus is a man's name
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: A man without end feels sick on a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: This British territory is one of the Leeward Islands in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Revolutionaries cut Che once for concealing these arms

indicators.note: concealing means the letters lie within the run of words before it

explanation.surface: Guerrillas once slashed Guevara to hide their weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints Che, as in Che Guevara; 'arms' are heraldic, not weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: An escutcheon is the shield on which a coat of arms is displayed.

clue.text: Find our case left going around — here?

definitions.text: Find our case left going around — here?

indicators.note: going around suggests the letters circulate into a new order

explanation.surface: An air traveller wondering where to collect a suitcase that is circling unclaimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' rearranges OUR CASE into CAROUSE, then L follows; the whole clue describes the airport belt.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage is collected from a rotating belt in the arrivals hall.

clue.text: Sad time before Havana's changed direction, perhaps

indicators.note: changed direction tells us the word for a Havana runs the other way

parts.note: a Havana is a Cuban cigar

explanation.surface: A gloomy moment before Cuba's capital alters its policy.
explanation.walkthrough: Havana looks like the city but is the cigar named after it, reversed to RAGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something calamitous or deeply sorrowful is called tragic.

clue.text: Manual worker who may pull out all the stops

definitions.text: Manual worker who may pull out all the stops

parts.words: Manual worker who may pull out all the stops
parts.note: a manual is a keyboard of a pipe instrument and stops are its knobs, so this player literally pulls them out

explanation.surface: A labourer who will make every effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A church musician plays the manuals and draws the stops of the instrument.

clue.text: Joint went down rapidly in US dock

parts.note: in American English the past tense of dive is dove
a dock is the stump of an animal's tail

explanation.surface: A joint plunged in an American harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' looks like a harbour but is a cut tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is an interlocking woodworking joint.

clue.text: Attractive person became the woman's home help

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
was stands for became, as in 'it was dark' at nightfall
her means the woman's

explanation.surface: A good-looking person turned into her domestic help.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish-cleaning appliance is a labour-saving helper in a kitchen.

clue.text: Sycophant dropping a name in glib speech

indicators.note: dropping here means falling into the speech, so the other letters go inside it

parts.note: a spiel is a slick patter

explanation.surface: A flatterer who drops names during smooth patter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping a name' suggests name-dropping, but the A and N are dropped into SPIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A fawning person is likened to a dog that grovels, so a toady is called a spaniel.

clue.text: Presuming tarragon goes into a stew

indicators.note: to be in a stew is to be in a mess, so the herb's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cook boldly adding herbs to a casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like cooking but means a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Presuming means overconfident or haughty.

clue.text: Person who embellishes home with plain gold

parts.note: in means at home
flat means plain or level
or is heraldic gold

explanation.surface: A decorator furnishing a house in simple gilt.
explanation.definitionFit: One who exaggerates puffs up the facts.

clue.text: One thus dead can be cut off

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
so means thus
the late means the dead

explanation.surface: A single person, so lifeless, can be severed.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to separate or sever from others.

clue.text: Cheap way to travel, always in coach

indicators.note: in places the poetic word for always inside the coach

parts.note: a stage is a stagecoach
e'er is poetic for ever, always

explanation.surface: Budget travel is always by bus.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest-priced passenger accommodation on a ship was in steerage.

clue.text: Spotty creature, youth given year prison sentence

parts.note: a lad is a youth
bird is British slang for a jail term, from rhyming slang bird-lime, time

explanation.surface: A pimply young man jailed for a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotty' suggests acne, but means spotted; bird is British slang for prison time.
explanation.definitionFit: This beetle has a red back with black spots.

clue.text: Container, for a small charge, left at Victoria

definitions.text: Container, for a small charge, left at Victoria

parts.words: Container, for a small charge, left at Victoria
parts.note: in Wilde's comedy a baby was found in a bag deposited at the Victoria station cloakroom, which charged a small fee

explanation.surface: Something checked into a station cloakroom for a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a London rail station; in The Importance of Being Earnest the hero was found in one there.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's bag was the receptacle famously left at the station cloakroom in Wilde's play.

clue.text: An English breed? That's totally ridiculous

definitions.text: An English breed? That's totally ridiculous

parts.words: An English breed? That's totally ridiculous
parts.note: calling this cattle or terrier breed English is absurd, since its name is a Scottish city

explanation.surface: Someone scoffing at the suggestion that a breed is English.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aberdeen Angus cattle and Aberdeen terrier are named after a city in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed names Aberdeen Angus and Aberdeen terrier come from a Scottish city.

clue.text: Son has picked up fabric on the way out

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the word is lifted and reads upward

parts.note: serge is a woollen cloth

explanation.surface: A boy collects cloth as he leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns SERGE upward to EGRES; S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a means of leaving.

clue.text: Devil of a girl that's willing

parts.note: Polly is a girl's name
on means willing, as in 'I'm on'

explanation.surface: A girl so eager she is a little devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollyon is the destroying angel of Revelation, a name for Satan.

clue.text: Home right beside centre of Hampstead area

indicators.note: beside centre of puts the letter next to the middle of the place name

parts.note: Hampstead Heath is a large park in north London

explanation.surface: A house on the right next to central Hampstead.
explanation.walkthrough: HAMPSTEAD HEATH is a London park; R sits beside its middle letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside stands for the household, so hearth and home are paired.

clue.text: Queen, beaten by Romans, taking a risk with snake around

indicators.note: around tells us the snake encircles the other letters

parts.note: a boa is a constricting snake
to dice, as in dice with death, is to take a risk

explanation.surface: A warrior queen defeated by Rome, gambling with a serpent coiled about her.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iceni queen, usually Boudicca now, rebelled against Roman Britain and lost.
explanation.definitionFit: This British tribal ruler led a revolt against Rome in AD 60–61 and was defeated.

clue.text: In retreat without ally, surely becoming exhausted

indicators.note: without means the friend's word is left out of the next word

parts.note: really can mean surely, as in 'really, you can't mean it'
tiring means growing weary

explanation.surface: Falling back without support, someone is certainly wearing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes ALLY from REALLY, leaving RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone retiring is withdrawing or pulling back.

clue.text: Delivered first from East in case containing many

indicators.note: containing means the case word holds the next letter

parts.note: lest means in case
D is 500 in Roman numerals, so many

explanation.surface: A parcel arrived first from the East inside a case holding many items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered first' means born first, the first child delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: The firstborn of several children is the oldest.
